scenes.heading: Transformations and symmetry
scenes.sub: Slide it, flip it, turn it
scenes.say: Video game characters slide and spin across the screen. Butterflies and logos have perfect symmetry. Let's learn the three moves that make it all happen.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Slide, flip or spin a sticker on a table
scenes.science: Translation, reflection, rotation: same size and shape
scenes.breaks: flip a real sticker and you see its sticky back. A reflected shape just becomes its mirror image.
scenes.say: Imagine a sticker on a table. You can slide it, flip it over, or spin it round a pin. That's a translation, a reflection and a rotation. The sticker never stretches or shrinks. Only its position changes.

scenes.heading: On the Cartesian plane
scenes.say: On the Cartesian plane: to translate, add to x to move right and add to y to move up. Reflect in the x-axis and y changes sign. Reflect in the y-axis and x changes sign. Rotate a half turn about the origin and both signs change.

scenes.heading: Translation
scenes.question: Translate A(−1, 4) 3 units right and 6 units down.
scenes.say: Translate the point negative one, four, three right and six down. Right three: negative one plus three is two. Down six: four minus six is negative two. So A dash is two, negative two.
scenes.caption: Translate A(−1, 4) 3 right and 6 down. Right 3: −1 + 3 = 2. Down 6: 4 − 6 = −2. So A′ is (2, −2).

scenes.heading: Rotation
scenes.question: Rotate C(4, 1) by 90° clockwise about the origin.
scenes.say: Rotate four, one by ninety degrees clockwise about the origin. The rule is x, y becomes y, negative x. So the image is one, negative four. It's moved from the top right quadrant to the bottom right, a quarter turn clockwise.
scenes.caption: Rotate C(4, 1) by 90° clockwise about the origin. The rule: (x, y) → (y, −x). So C′ is (1, −4).

scenes.heading: Two kinds of symmetry

right.title: Rotational symmetry
points: Order = fits in a full turn

scenes.say: Line symmetry means you can fold the shape so the halves match. A rectangle has two lines, a square has four. Rotational symmetry means it fits onto itself as you turn it. The order is how many times it fits in a full turn. A square has order four.

points: Image is congruent to the object
scenes.say: Quick recap. Translation slides, reflection flips, rotation turns. The image stays the same size and shape. In the x-axis mirror, y changes sign. Order of rotation is the number of fits in a full turn. Now try the practice questions!
